entries.03308d4e96b8db36: This core business operates scheduled passenger and cargo shipping routes linking the Tokyo Islands and the mainland, and sightseeing cruises within Tokyo Bay. Consolidated subsidiary Ogasawara Kaiun operates the scheduled route linking Tokyo and Ogasawara (Chichijima), Izu Shichito Kaiun handles cargo transport, and consolidated subsidiaries on each island provide shipping agency services, onboard services and ship repair centered on jetfoil maintenance. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥12,482 million.

entries.21782ea22fcc4044: A shipping company centered on passenger and cargo routes connecting Tokyo with the Izu Islands and the Ogasawara Islands, which also operates trading and food and beverage, hotels, and passenger motor vehicle transport.
entries.26437de817f037c1: It handles the everyday travel of island residents and the transport of daily necessities, and also provides a base for tourists' trips and for accommodation and travel on the islands.
entries.2937a5b00a495aa9: It has operated island routes since 1907, when it began mandated routes under a contract with the Governor of Tokyo Prefecture, and has a group structure with consolidated subsidiaries acting as shipping agents on each island, providing integrated service from passenger and cargo transport to accommodation and transport on the islands. Other features include short-time transport between Tokyo and Oshima and Kozushima by the high-speed jetfoil, and a long-distance route linking Tokyo and Chichijima operated by consolidated subsidiary Ogasawara Kaiun.

entries.3a831b9f64681537: This is a business model in which it carries passengers and daily necessities on regular routes linking the Tokyo Islands and the mainland, and earns revenue by combining food and beverage and merchandise sales on board and at waiting rooms with a hotel and bus business on Oshima.

entries.5fabd2dee2ce1575: The basic management policy is to contribute to regional communities by fulfilling the public mission of the passenger routes linking the Tokyo Islands and the mainland as island and daily-life routes, and the responsibility of safely and reliably transporting daily necessities by cargo routes. As a long-term strategy, under a policy of building a low-cost management structure that is not affected by income fluctuations through flexible costs and reduced fixed costs, it will work on off-peak measures and periodic replacement and fleet restructuring of vessels, and strengthen sales activities not bound by existing methods, such as new product development and full-scale rollout of the ＥＣ site business. For 2026, under the slogan 'Ｂｕｉｌｄｉｎｇ　Ｔｒｕｓｔ２０２６', with thorough safe operation and strengthened compliance systems as the foundation, it states that it will strive to enhance corporate value, with restoring and improving trust as its top priority.
entries.6edd49278af47795: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥14,288 million, down 2.2% from ¥14,604 million in the previous year. External customer revenue by segment was ¥12,482 million for the shipping-related business, ¥1,182 million for the Commercial Food and Beverage Business, ¥345 million for the Hotel Business and ¥278 million for the passenger automobile transport business.

entries.9e89bac6843a499e: Established in 1889, it is listed on the Standard Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It has 11 consolidated subsidiaries, and consolidated employees numbered 377 as of December 31, 2025. Its head office is located in Kaigan, Minato-ku, Tokyo.
entries.9ecf158b73dcb828: The company's routes have a public character as island and daily-life routes, and include routes covered by the Ritō Kōro Seibi Hō (Remote Island Shipping Route Development Act), which the company states must be maintained on public-interest grounds even though they are unprofitable. The company states that the Tokyo Islands are experiencing advancing population decline, cargo transport volumes are on a gradual downward trend, and the business environment remains severe.
entries.9f2b8fc7eb787570: Profit attributable to owners of parent for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥368 million. The previous year's profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥293 million.

entries.d8fe8f18a2047141: In the fiscal year ended December 2025, the effect of the fare revision carried out two years earlier, which applied for the full year on the main Izu Islands route, supported earnings. Meanwhile, passenger numbers declined due to reduced vessels and sailings during the peak summer season and a switch to moored operation of summer cooling boats in Tokyo Bay, and cargo volumes continued to decline gradually amid population decline in the island regions. The recovery in tourism demand has been slower than in central Tokyo, and the company states that passenger volumes continue to fall short of pre-pandemic levels.
